filter_note: V1 set (7) + market briefing + AI news; Today window = Thu Nov 26 (after the morning run) – Fri Nov 27 morning PT (US Thanksgiving and Black Friday; items already on the Nov 26 and earlier briefs not re-led)

market_briefing.lede: AI shopping traffic jumped over Thanksgiving, but agents still complete few purchases themselves, and the week's security news centred on stolen access tokens rather than model failures.

bullets.text: Nov 26–27: Adobe told the AP that traffic from AI services to US retail sites more than doubled on Thanksgiving year over year; Bain research puts purchases made by AI agents at 0.4% of global e-commerce transactions, and a Morning Consult poll for Visa found 23% of adults trust generative AI to pay for them.

Nov 26: SAP confirmed a security incident and says it has found no sign of access to customer business data. An insider told Der Spiegel that attackers used stolen employee access tokens to copy and change SAP source code on GitHub, possibly with agentic AI; SAP has not confirmed those details.

biggest_ai_news.title: OpenAI fixes a GPT-6.2 billing error; limits arrive sooner
biggest_ai_news.body: Posted late Nov 25 PT, reported Nov 26: a launch bug had under-counted GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol usage. Users now hit limits 40% faster on Astra and 25% faster on Sol than last week; no back-charges, and one banked reset for Go, Plus, Pro and Business.

biggest_ai_news.title: Nvidia pauses server shipments to four Southeast Asian countries
biggest_ai_news.body: Nov 26: per the WSJ, Nvidia told Dell, Super Micro and other partners to pause shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia while it checks compliance with US export rules.

biggest_ai_news.title: An AI agent pays by bank at Papa John's in a UK pilot
biggest_ai_news.body: Nov 27: TrueLayer's pilot with Lloyds and NatWest, run in the FCA's sandbox, lets Papa John's agent take payment from a bank account within spending limits the customer sets with the bank.

what_changed.title: Benioff posts Salesforce's Cyber Week day-two numbers
what_changed.body: Nov 26: Marc Benioff posted 12.6M Agentforce AI conversations and actions, 14B Marketing Cloud messages and $1.15B in Commerce GMV for Cyber Week day two, with '100% reliability' (company-reported; the post does not say whether the figures are cumulative). His day-one post (Nov 25) listed 5.57M agent conversations and actions and $554M GMV.

what_changed.title: OpenAI corrects GPT-6.2 usage metering
what_changed.body: Late Nov 25 PT: Codex lead Thibault Sottiaux said a launch billing mistake discounted GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol usage; after the fix, the same work uses 40% (Astra) and 25% (Sol) more of a plan's allowance than last week. OpenAI is adding one banked reset and not charging for past usage.

what_changed.title: SAP confirms a security incident
what_changed.body: Nov 26: SAP said it identified suspicious activity and found no sign of access to customer business data. Der Spiegel's insider account (stolen employee tokens used to copy and change source code on GitHub) is unconfirmed by SAP. The same day, Germany's BSI warned about autonomous AI attack tools.

quiet_note: No launch, funding, M&A or pricing change from Gong, Clay, Nooks, Outreach, Salesloft or Monaco dated Nov 26–27 (US Thanksgiving and Black Friday). Monaco's blog posted two tool-comparison guides and Sam Blond's X activity was replies and retweets; no new Clay changelog entry.

market_direction.label: Accelerating (AI-referred shopping traffic)
market_direction.text: AI traffic to US retail sites more than doubled on Thanksgiving (Adobe), and Benioff's day-two post put Agentforce at 12.6M conversations and actions (Nov 26).

market_direction.label: Steady (agents that pay)
market_direction.text: Agent purchases are 0.4% of global e-commerce transactions (Bain); payment pilots like TrueLayer's run under regulator watch (Nov 27).

market_direction.label: Accelerating (tighter metering of model usage)
market_direction.text: OpenAI's GPT-6.2 billing fix (Nov 25–26) follows its shared Chat and Work meter (Nov 25).

market_direction.label: Steady (Gong, Clay, Nooks, Outreach, Salesloft, Monaco)
market_direction.text: No announcements of their own Nov 26–27 over the holiday.

language_pulse.gloss: OpenAI's saved, one-time reset of a ChatGPT usage limit, given after the GPT-6.2 billing fix (Nov 26).
TrueLayer's term for an AI agent paying from a bank account under bank-set spending limits (Nov 27).

competitive_moves.text: Benioff posted Cyber Week day-two figures: 12.6M Agentforce AI conversations and actions, 14B Marketing Cloud messages, $1.15B Commerce GMV (Nov 26).

watch.title: Wed Dec 2: Salesforce Q3 FY27 results
watch.body: Results after the close, call 2:00 PM PT. Watch for full Cyber Week Agentforce numbers after Benioff's day-one and day-two posts, and any adoption figures for Salesforce in Claude.

interpretation.fact: Nov 26 Benioff posted Cyber Week day-two numbers (12.6M Agentforce conversations and actions, $1.15B Commerce GMV). Late Nov 25 PT OpenAI said it fixed a GPT-6.2 billing error, so Astra and Sol limits arrive 40% and 25% sooner. Nov 26 SAP confirmed a security incident and Nvidia paused server shipments to four Southeast Asian countries (WSJ via TechCrunch). Nov 27 TrueLayer announced an agent pay-by-bank pilot with Papa John's. Adobe, Bain and Visa data show AI shopping traffic up sharply but agent purchases small. Gong, Clay, Nooks, Outreach, Salesloft and Monaco announced nothing new Nov 26–27.
interpretation.interpretation: Agents are now a big source of traffic and conversations but a small share of completed transactions; the gap is about trust, payment controls and access tokens, which is also where buyers of sales agents will push vendors.

feed.summary: Marc Benioff posted Salesforce's Cyber Week day-two numbers: 12.6M Agentforce AI conversations and actions, 14B Marketing Cloud messages and $1.15B in Commerce GMV.
